headline: Weekend · Aug 14–16: Awarapan 2 Storms Independence Day, Spider-Man Rewrites India's Record Books
dek: Emraan Hashmi's comeback opens at ~₹21 Cr — triple Batwara 1947 — while Suriya's Vishwanath and Sons roars in at ₹15 Cr and Spider-Man becomes the biggest Hollywood film in Indian history. The Friday-led Top 10 to Aug 16, the audience-demographics split, the fortnight's holdovers and OTT, and how our pre-release calls graded.

headline: Microdramas Are a $7.8B Format. Streaming’s Real Response Will Be Billing, Not Shorter Content.
dek: The 90-second vertical format has quietly overtaken China’s box office and grown 4× in the US in twelve months. India’s market runs to 100M users. But Pocket FM just exited despite the boom, and the reason it did explains what Netflix and Prime will do next. Boxoffy analysis.

headline: Spider-Man: Brand New Day Review — 3.5/5, Emotional Over Masala
dek: Guest FDFS review by @iamashishsrrk (POSITIVE FAN), one of Indian cinema Twitter’s most trusted voices: a character-first Spidey with one roof-lifting Hulk moment. Plus how it sits with the record ₹60.60 Cr India Day 1.

headline: Weekend Preview: Spider-Man Owns Aug 1–3, Chasing Endgame's India Records
dek: Brand New Day turns the weekend into a one-film show, tracking to the biggest Hollywood opening India has ever seen. Plus how the holdovers hold up, the estimated Top 10, this week's OTT moves, and Ramayana + Batwara on the horizon.

headline: Spider-Man: Brand New Day — The Loudest Week in the World
dek: Record-breaking presales, a China release No Way Home never got, and a bull case that puts the global opening past $700M and US past $300M. Boxoffy on the hype, the Tobey-to-Tom record arc, and why India could speed to a ₹60 crore day one.

headline: Batwara 1947 vs Awarapan 2: The Independence Day Rematch
dek: Nineteen years after Apne beat Awarapan six to one, Sunny Deol and Emraan Hashmi clash again on Aug 14. A Boxoffy Hype Index on both films — the run-rates, the YouTube ground read, presales vs day-of mechanics, BCM day-1 projections, and what each campaign must do to build hype.

headline: Toxic Wants To Be India's Next Global Crossover
dek: Yash's KGF-2 follow-up has the English cut, the festive worldwide date, and Fandango already pushing the trailer to US audiences — but no international distributor is named yet. A Boxoffy Hype Index on the crossover gamble, the actor-producer carrying the risk, and how Toxic feeds into Ramayana in November.

headline: The Odyssey Gave IMAX Its Biggest Weekend Ever. Round Two Starts Friday.
dek: $52M from IMAX in three days — a fifth of a $264.1M global bow and the format's biggest opening on record. Plus the national top 10, how our Jul 17–19 calls scored, Jana Nayagan's Day 1, the OTT queue, and the Aug 14 Batwara 1947 vs Awarapan 2 rematch.

headline: Ajay Devgn: The Complete Box-Office Ledger — 108 Films, ₹4,160 Cr, ~60 Cr Tickets
dek: Every film, every verdict, every rupee and ticket, 1991–2026 — the full career record of Bollywood's Singham. Career ~₹4,160 Cr India net and ~60 Cr footfalls, led by Tanhaji (₹279.4 Cr / 2.22 Cr tickets). Four distinct eras, a volatile 2020s that still crossed ₹1,000 Cr post-COVID, and the inflation-proof footfall math behind it all. BOI + Sacnilk sourced, BCM-modeled where public data is light.

headline: Weekend Preview · July 17–19: The Odyssey Takes World Cinema and Every IMAX, Dhamaal 4 Holds, Samantha Storms OTT
dek: Christopher Nolan's Odyssey opens #1 in India (~₹15–17.5 Cr Day 1, his biggest-ever Indian bow, past Oppenheimer) and the US (~$115–118M) at once, sweeping the IMAX and premium screens in both markets. Dhamaal 4 holds the family crowd past ₹100 Cr net while Welcome to the Jungle and Alpha fade under the wave. Plus a to-scale IMAX 70mm vs Dolby vs 35mm format explainer, our last-weekend scorecard (we called Dhamaal 4's ₹13.75 Cr open), the full US board, and the week's OTT slate led by Samantha's Maa Inti Bangaaram.

headline: The Odyssey BCM Hype Index — One Week Out: Reviews Are In, and the Opening Number Gets Honest

The first critic reactions are glowing, so we firm the BCM Hype Index from 92 to 94 — but trade tracking ($80–132M) lands below our May opening base, so we revise the debut down to ~$108M and reframe the whole call as a legs-and-lifetime play. India ₹220–280 Cr base case holds; revised $0.9–1.45B worldwide range.

headline: Alpha Opens Well Despite a Negative Campaign, Welcome to the Jungle Keeps Running, and Main Vaapas Aaunga Continues Its Dream Run

headline: Why the Movie Industry Loves Nostalgia: The Formula Behind the Feeling
dek: If story is the art, nostalgia is the formula underneath it. From Gadar 2's ₹525 Cr on middling reviews to Top Gun: Maverick, from the reminiscence bump to the Friends rerun economy and YouTube's personalised time machine: a deep dive into why audiences pay big to go back — and what Proust, Ishiguro and Toni Morrison understood long before any studio ran a focus group.

headline: Gadar vs Lagaan, 25 Years On: The Greatest Box-Office Clash in Hindi Cinema History
dek: On 15 June 2001, Gadar: Ek Prem Katha and Lagaan opened the very same Friday — and, almost impossibly, both became hits. A data-led Rewind on the era, the openings, the budgets and the verdicts, with a 2001-vs-2025 reality check and a first-person memory from Indore.

headline: Trailer Hype Index: Cocktail 2, Welcome to the Jungle & Alpha — Opening Predictions

headline: What Is a Screenplay — and Why a Screenwriter Isn't Just a "Writer"

headline: Box Office Weekend Recap — May 29–31, 2026: Two YouTubers Took the Top 2 in Hollywood. Mandalorian Got Walked Off. India's Chart Went Mollywood-Marathi-Tamil.
dek: Belated but complete recap (PB was traveling). Before we get to India, we have to talk about Hollywood: A24's Backrooms opens $81M directed by a 20-year-old. Obsession crossed $100M domestic after growing in BOTH W2 +30% AND W3 +10% — first film since E.T. 1982 to pull that off. Mandalorian & Grogu cratered -69% W2, the steepest Star Wars second-weekend drop ever recorded. Two YouTubers punching 1 and 2. Star Wars walked off the field. Then to India: Drishyam 3 crosses ₹100 Cr (6th Malayalam ever), Karuppu is now Suriya's biggest grosser, Deool Band 2 hits 340% ROI on a ₹10 Cr Marathi budget, Bhooth Bangla holds W7 at ₹195 Cr India. BCM v1.3 verified across 12 sources.

headline: The Emergency Years at the Box Office — 21 Months That Reshaped Hindi Cinema
dek: Boxoffy Archive Series. Between June 1975 and March 1977, Hindi cinema worked under content regulation that capped action sequences at 90 seconds. Sholay's ending was censored. Aandhi was banned mid-release. Kissa Kursi Ka's prints were physically burned. Cinema halls stayed full anyway. The multi-starrer format became dominant. Soviet Union was the largest overseas market. Ticket prices, production houses, currency context, and the full release-by-release box office archive.

headline: Before the Crore Club — How Indian Box Office Began (1913–1943)
